s.t:
ServiceNow is seeking a Partner Technology Architect to serve as the primary strategic interface for our Global and Strategic Regional partners. In this role, you will drive holistic partner growth through pre-sales technical excellence, business development, solution strategy, and AI-first technology adoption.

You will combine trusted advisory relationships with partner executives, industry-aligned solution architecture, and go-to-market leadership into a single accountable role — translating platform capabilities, AI innovation, and industry context into repeatable, outcome-driven offerings that partners can build, scale, and monetize.
While this role expands into strategic business development and co-innovation, pre-sales technical excellence remains the primary operational foundation — including technical discovery, solution demonstrations, proof-of-concept leadership, and architectural validation that accelerates partner-led customer engagements.

As a Partner Technology Architect, you will serve as the dedicated strategic counterpart for assigned partner organizations, owning the full spectrum from pre-sales technical engagement through strategic co-innovation and business growth advisory.
Partner Strategy & Business Development
Serve as the primary strategic interface for assigned partners, building trusted relationships with partner executives and practice leaders.
Lead joint business planning to align partner investments, industry focus, and go-to-market priorities across all routes to market.
Advise partners on practice growth, specialization strategy, and readiness for AI-enabled offerings.
Influence partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline through offer-led strategy and solution differentiation.
Pre-Sales Excellence & Solution Strategy
Lead and support technical discovery sessions, executive briefings, and solution demonstrations that articulate platform value and accelerate partner-led deal velocity.
Drive solution strategy, helping partners align offerings to high-value industry workflows and customer outcomes.
Translate platform and AI capabilities into partner-differentiated, scalable solutions at the conceptual and architectural level.
Maintain strong workflow fluency across enterprise domains including CRM, IT, Security, and Business Services.
Design and execute partner-led proofs of concept and co-demonstrations that prove business value, technical feasibility, and competitive differentiation.
Provide technical escalation support for critical partner-led opportunities, ensuring partners have access to deep expertise at key deal milestones.
AI-First Innovation & Co-Creation
Champion AI-first solution design, including intelligent workflows, automation, and agent-based use cases.
Orchestrate partner engagement with Partner Solution Architects and domain-specialist advisors (AI, CRM, Security & Risk) to accelerate solution development.
Ensure partner offerings progress from concept through validation to scalable commercialization.
Promote responsible, enterprise-ready AI adoption aligned to governance and trust standards.
Value Engineering & Orchestration
Connect solution strategy to measurable business outcomes including efficiency, growth, ROI, and time-to-value.
Support executive-level conversations with clear value narratives and outcome-based storytelling.
Coordinate across internal specialist teams to deliver a unified partner experience, not fragmented touchpoints.

s.h: What you need to be successful in this role
s.t:
8+ years of experience in pre-sales solution consulting, partner strategy, enterprise technology advisory, or related roles with proven success leading technical discovery, demonstrations, and partner engagements.
Proven experience working directly with partners, system integrators, hyperscalers, or technology alliances.
Strong executive presence with the ability to influence senior partner stakeholders at VP+ level.
Demonstrated ability to connect business strategy, industry context, and technology solutions into actionable partner growth plans.
Experience shaping or scaling partner practices, offerings, or go-to-market motions.
Solid understanding of enterprise platforms and workflow-based solutions at the conceptual and architectural level.
Working knowledge of AI-enabled use cases, automation patterns, and data-driven workflows.
Deep familiarity with at least one industry vertical (e.g., Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Public Sector).
Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving.

Experience with ServiceNow platform and AI capabilities (Now Assist, AI Agents).
Background in management consulting, strategy advisory, or partner business development.
ServiceNow certifications (e.g., CSA, CIS, or architectural certifications).
Experience across multiple partner routes to market (C&I, MSP, Reseller, Hyperscaler, Build).
Familiarity with competitive platforms and ability to articulate ServiceNow differentiation.
What This Role Does Not Do
Perform platform configuration, development, or solution delivery.
Manage commercial contracts, pricing, or financial program management.
Replace deep technical or implementation specialist roles (leverages domain-specialist advisors and Partner Solution Architects for depth).
Own day-to-day partner relationship management (coordinates with Partner Management).
Travel for partner, customer, and organizational activities up to 50%.

An overview of this role As the Manager, Solutions Architects for our Enterprise team in the San Francisco Bay area, you'll lead a distributed group of intermediate and senior Solutions Architects serving enterprise customers in the West sales territory.

You'll guide your team to act as trusted advisors to GitLab prospects and customers, helping them validate GitLab 's Enterprise Edition as the right technical and business solution and supporting successful adoption of the GitLab platform across the entire software development lifecycle.

You'll hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team, set clear expectations, and be accountable for how your team runs complex technical evaluations, articulates business outcomes, and collaborates with Sales, Engineering, Product Management, and Marketing.

You'll model the work of a Solutions Architect yourself, from solution design through technical presentations, so your team is equipped to drive meaningful customer change with GitLab . What you'll do Lead a distributed team of intermediate and senior Solutions Architects supporting Enterprise customers in the West territory.

Coach, mentor, and develop team members through regular feedback, career support, and skills development in both technical and consultative areas. Grow and retain a high-performing team by hiring thoughtfully, onboarding effectively, and fostering an inclusive, results-focused culture.

Guide by example by engaging in key customer opportunities as a Solutions Architect, from discovery through technical validation and successful adoption of the GitLab platform.

Drive the quality and consistency of technical evaluations, demos, and proofs of concept so that GitLab solutions clearly address customer business and technical requirements. Collaborate closely with regional sales managers on territory strategy, account planning, and forecast support to ensure alignment between technical and commercial motions.

Partner with Product Management, Engineering, and Marketing to share field insights, influence the roadmap, and improve messaging around GitLab 's Enterprise Edition and platform capabilities.

Own team execution by defining and tracking key performance indicators, and communicate progress, risks, and priorities clearly to your team, peers, and leadership. What you'll bring Experience mentoring and developing technical team members, including giving and receiving constructive feedback.

Experience managing or leading technical pre-sales or information technology professionals, ideally in an enterprise-focused environment. Ability to collaborate effectively with other managers and cross-functional partners to plan and execute sales and go-to-market strategies.

Strong technical presentation and communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and business stakeholders. Knowledge of the end-to-end software development lifecycle, including modern software development or operations practices.

Understanding of continuous integration and continuous deployment concepts and their impact on customer outcomes. Familiarity with cloud computing concepts, related technologies, and common customer adoption patterns.

Ability and willingness to travel in line with business needs and the company's travel policy, and openness to learning and using GitLab and related tools, including through transferable experience from adjacent domains.

About the team The Enterprise Solutions Architect team partners with our largest customers to design and validate technical solutions that drive successful adoption of the GitLab platform.

This role leads a group of intermediate and senior Solutions Architects aligned to the West Enterprise sales territory, working closely with Sales, Engineering, Product Management, and Marketing to support complex evaluations and long-term customer outcomes.

We operate in a fully remote, asynchronous way across North America, using GitLab and our handbook-first approach to stay aligned on strategy, share technical best practices, and continuously improve how we support the sales cycle.

Key opportunities for our team include deepening technical adoption of GitLab Enterprise Edition, connecting customer business goals with architectural recommendations, and serving as strong product advocates in the field. ServiceNow is seeking Enterprise Architects to join our UK&I Team. The Enterprise Architecture Team is part of our pre-sales solution consulting organisation focused on building credibility and trust with the technical leaders in our largest customers by developing cross-functional strategies and solutions.

Our team brings technical expertise, real-world experience, strong executive engagement skills and an inspirational mindset to help our customers understand the opportunities of the “platform of platforms” vision. We act as technical leaders for our customers most complex solutions, designed to ensure that they can realize the value they need.

We do this by leveraging best practice and industry standards to build customer trust and architect best in class solutions.
While collaborating with customers, partners, and the wider ServiceNow sales team, the right candidate will create and communicate high-level architectures and strategies that are both written and verbal, to audiences up to and including the CIO/CTO level.

The Enterprise Architect will articulate the advantage of ServiceNow being built on a single cloud platform consisting of a single user interface, one code base and one data model.

The Enterprise Architect will also lead and participate in the delivery of workshops, best practice overviews, and educational sessions to existing customers and partners.

s.h: What you get to do in this role
s.t:
Engage with customer executives in the Enterprise Industry team which comprises manufacturing, retail, travel and service companies.
Identify pain points and opportunities to deliver value and then translate them into solutions from ServiceNow
Work in a fast moving and dynamic sales environment with a range of customer, colleagues and partners to help them understand the power of the Now platform and the potential opportunities of the future of work
Lead architecture and design engagements to demonstrate how ServiceNow meets the needs of strategic customers, including Customer Experience, AI Governance, Autonomous, IT Transformation, Digital Products/Services, Platform as a Service, Enterprise Service Management, and the co-creation of industry specific solutions.
Understand the business and digital strategy of the customer and articulate how ServiceNow can enable and deliver value to their organization, seamlessly integrating into their current and future technology landscape
Understand the detail behind the ServiceNow and platform of platforms architecture and communicate it at various levels
Work with architecture development methods, modelling approaches and architecture patterns for integration
Influence and impact at multiple levels within a customer account (Enterprise Architects, Domain Architects, Directors, VPs, and CXOs) and maintain these relationships throughout their customer journey.
Provide thought leadership and collaborate with internal ServiceNow business units
Identify, lead and contribute to the creation of best practices, white papers, workshops, etc

s.h: To be successful in this role you have

Deep experience (8+ years) of working in Manufacturing, Retail or Service Industries in a strategic and consultative architecture presales role.
Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
Familiarity with enterprise systems architecture (ERP, MES, WMS, POS, digital commerce platforms)
Knowledge of major ERP and enterprise software vendors in manufacturing and retail (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Shopify, etc.)

Deep understanding of trends like: Supply chain digitalization, inventory optimization, omnichannel retail, lean manufacturing, Industry 4.0, predictive analytics, and demand-driven planning
Passion and energy for building business relationships and is accustomed to driving the simplification of complex concepts into compelling customer proposals
Drive for results using out-of-the-box innovative thinking together with excellent problem-solving skills
An intrinsic ability to understand and prioritize work and is willing to make big bets when the time is right, to invest time and energy in the right areas.
Willingness to jump-in and roll-up their sleeves alongside customers, colleagues and partners to get things done faster and better.
10 or more years of proven success in influencing senior technology leaders to drive change in a pre-sales, customer, or delivery focused role.
A track record of success in using Human Centered Design techniques to explore the customers current reality and set a vision for the future.
Expertise designing, implementing and managing advanced architectures in an application domain and integrating multiple systems or platforms
Experience with Enterprise Architecture or Application Architecture pre-sales in a software vendor or professional services environment.

Understanding of the business/financial model of manufacturing and retail organizations
Understanding of supply chain economics and retail business models
Understanding of regulations in manufacturing and retail (data privacy, environmental compliance, import/export)
Practical experience with vendors in the Manufacturing and Retail software space
Practical experience with ISV and software vendors relevant to the industry and customer.
Excellent understanding of the architectural principles for cloud-based platforms that include SaaS, PaaS, multi-tenancy, and automation
Experience and understanding of multiple technical domains - application, data, DevOps, AI/ML, integration, big data, mobility, analytics, etc.
Intrinsically curious and passionate about researching current and emerging technologies and developing innovative solutions
Experience presenting architecture concepts, designs, and goals to technology leaders and partners

About Zuora
At Zuora, we help businesses grow smarter and adapt faster. Our platform powers modern business models — from subscriptions and usage-based pricing to AI-driven and outcome-based offerings — helping companies launch new products, automate complex billing, and unlock predictable, recurring revenue.
We’ve led the Subscription Economy for more than a decade. Now we’re evolving again by building the definitive platform for quote to cash and helping companies monetize their products and services with an adaptable, AI-ready foundation.
The Opportunity
As a Zuora Enterprise Solution Architect (ESA), you will be a trusted partner and advisor to live, already-implemented customers. This role is focused on maximizing the value of Zuora solutions by aligning them with customers’ strategic goals, optimizing Order-to-Revenue operations, and driving measurable business outcomes.

You will deliver customized roadmaps, lead strategic workshops, and provide ongoing optimizations to ensure that Zuora’s platform continues to meet customers’ evolving needs.

Acting as a key strategist, you’ll guide customers through challenges and opportunities, helping them unlock the full potential of Zuora to support their long-term growth and success.

Strategy Alignment
Collaborate with customers to understand their business objectives and develop phased, actionable roadmaps tailored to their strategic goals.
Design scalable solutions that evolve with customers’ growth, ensuring long-term value creation and adaptability to changing business needs.
Prioritize frameworks that deliver measurable outcomes and align with best practices in subscription management and Order-to-Revenue processes.
Strategic Advisory & Insights
Serve as a trusted advisor, offering actionable insights into industry trends, best practices, and process optimizations.
Provide strategic guidance to help customers leverage Zuora for operational agility, enhanced efficiency, and competitive advantage.
Proactively identify opportunities for innovation and improvement, ensuring customers continuously extract value from Zuora.
Workshops & Optimization
Lead standardization workshops to assess and optimize configurations, workflows, and customizations, establishing scalable and efficient frameworks.
Facilitate detailed workshops to refine configurations, improve system performance, and streamline processes, delivering tailored recommendations to maximize ROI and user satisfaction.
Lead technical configuration and integration reviews and provide optimization recommendations.

5+ years of hands-on proficiency in Zuora Billing, Revenue, and CPQ modules, with expertise in designing scalable, impactful solutions.
10+ years of Domain-Specific Expertise: Experience with Billing and Revenue Management and ERP platforms such as SAP, Oracle, and NetSuite.
Proven ability to deliver customer-aligned roadmaps and provide strategic advisory that aligns with evolving business needs.
Integration Proficiency, strong understanding of REST and SOAP APIs, and ETL, with experience integrating with ERP, CRM, and core systems.
Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical, and communication skills with a customer-first approach.

Advanced Zuora Certifications: Strong hands-on proficiency in Zuora Billing, Revenue, and CPQ modules, supported by certifications like Zuora Billing Certified Consultant and Zuora Billing Delivery Architect.
Compliance Knowledge: Familiarity with GDPR, FISMA, ASC 606, and IFRS 15 compliance standards and their impact on revenue recognition.
Diverse Industry Experience: Ability to adapt solutions across various sectors, particularly in subscription management industries.
Global Project Leadership: Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects in international and cross-cultural settings.
Process Optimization: Expertise in leading workshops for standardization, configuration refinement, and process improvements to maximize ROI and efficiency.
Strategic Advisory Skills: Ability to provide actionable insights into industry trends, best practices, and operational strategies for long-term customer success.
Independent Consulting Acumen: Proven track record of self-directed consulting engagements, delivering results with minimal supervision.
Strong Collaboration: Skilled in leading cross-functional teams, driving collaboration, and ensuring the successful delivery of large-scale solutions.

As a member of our MyFitnessPal Engineering team, you’ll have the opportunity to positively impact those users with your expertise in the backend systems that drive the MyFitnessPal ecosystem. In addition to technical expertise, you’ll find that your teammates value collaboration, mentorship, and inclusive environments.

MyFitnessPal encourages innovation and adoption of the latest technologies available to deliver an amazing experience for our members.

Our diverse team of brilliant technologists builds and maintains native mobile applications, a web application, the world’s largest nutrition database, constantly evolving data science and AI/ML assets, the backend infrastructure and data platform required to support these applications and databases, as well as the business systems and data required to manage an awesome company.

Technologies and languages we work with include: Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, Git Hub, PlanetScale, Elasticsearch, Scala, Python, SQL, Amplitude, Appsflyer, Kubernetes, Kafka, Docker, Okta and Claude Code. We care more about your general engineering skills and technical leadership than your knowledge of a specific language and or framework.

Own the end-to-end systems design of the MyFitnessPal product data stack
Develop, drive, and maintain the systems architecture roadmap for the product data stack
Serve as the primary point of contact in Data Platform for the consolidated data stack, coordinating contributions from Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Product Analytics, and backend engineering teams
Define and enforce data movement and standardization discipline across the stack
Lead architecture review of new tool decisions, vetting vendors against the existing stack, surfacing duplication, and collaborating on proof-of-value evaluations
Contribute to the compliance architecture for user data, including PII tagging and a deletion/DSR policy by which every tool receiving user data is governed
Administer access and licensing across the data stack, maintaining a single view of spend and access
Document and evangelize architecture decisions, standards, and ownership models across the organization

Demonstrated experience defining architecture standards adopted across a team or organization, and enforcing them through automation rather than manual review
Cost-conscious ownership of infrastructure and vendor spend, balancing performance and reliability against cost

Our SAP platform is at a pivotal moment; moving to RISE, migrating to s/4, embracing Clean Core, and building the BTP foundations that will power our next decade of innovation. The Platform Architect is the person who connects all these dots: architecture, extensibility, developer enablement, and governance.

If you want to shape a global SAP landscape across a portfolio of iconic luxury Maisons, this is the role. HOW WILL YOU MAKE AN IMPACT?Within the SAP platform team, the SAP Platform Architect defines and governs the SAP platform architecture across S/4HANA (ERP, EWM, GTS-), SAP BTP, and all integration touchpoints.

Shaping the technology landscape, setting guardrails, and ensuring every extension or customisation is justified, sustainable, and future-proof.

You will lead the OSBF Design Authority, promote Clean Core principles and SAP-s extensibility strategy (side-by-side vs. in-app), and ensure alignment with both SAP-s product roadmap and our enterprise architecture. Your impact spans across a multi-stream technical roadmap covering 4 strategic pillars: 1.

Architecture Vision & Roadmap Own and drive the architectural direction of the platform across Core Architecture, BTP & Development.

Participate in strategic architectural decisions such as use cases for BTP, Federated platforms (Mendix, Tulip, Pega-), ERP/EWM decoupling, S/4HANA continuous evolution, including associated topics such as Job Scheduling or establishing a Printing Platform for the group.

Collaborate with the Enterprise Architecture team on cross-cutting concerns such as Disaster Recovery design and enterprise-wide technology alignment. Evolve the Platform to further integrate CI/CD practices. Integrate Richemont AI strategy in the platform roadmap & design.

Define consumable and reusable services for product teams that accelerate delivery, increase product teams- autonomy, and reduce the need for custom development, duplicated effort, and reliance on central platform expertise. 2.

Clean Core Governance & Extensibility Strategy Define and enforce Clean Core guidelines: minimise custom code, maximise standard, and leverage key-user extensibility and BTP side-by-side extensions.

Own the decision framework for -where to extend-: in-app (BAdIs, RAP, key-user extensibility) vs. side-by-side (CAP on BTP, Integration Suite, or Federated Platforms). Guide product teams on the right extensibility pattern for each use case. Conduct architecture reviews for all significant developments. 3.

Standards, Patterns & Guardrails Integrates Group Standards for reusable architecture patterns, in particular for API design and ownership, event-driven integration, data models, CDS views, and Fiori apps.

Champion configuration as Code for sap platforms, including BTP (Terraform) which adheres to Richemont guidelines in terms of security, Identity management and connectivity. Publish and maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and reference architectures.

Guide the technical archiving and data volume management strategy and application retirement (ILM). Provide architectural direction on data lifecycle decisions that impact platform performance, storage costs, and compliance. 4. Community & Enablement Participate in cross-team design reviews and lead the SAP platform Architecture Board.

Establish and animate an Architect Community across the product teams. Stay ahead of SAP technology evolution through continuous learning, SAP community engagement, and vendor dialogue. HOW WILL YOU EXPERIENCE SUCCESS WITH US?

Education & Experience 10+ years of progressive experience in SAP ecosystems, with deep expertise across S/4HANA, SAP BTP, and hybrid integration landscapes. 3+ years in an SAP platform architecture role. Master-s degree in computer science, engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Technical Expertise SAP S/4HANA: Deep understanding of S/4HANA architecture, Clean Core methodology, custom code analysis (ATC, Custom Code Migration app), and extensibility options (BAdIs, RAP, key-user extensibility).

SAP BTP: Strong knowledge of the BTP service portfolio - CAP, Integration Suite, SAP Build Work Zone, HANA Cloud, AI Core / Generative AI Hub, Event Mesh, Destination & Connectivity services. Architecture Patterns: Proven expertise in API-first design, event-driven architecture, side-by-side extensions, and Fiori/UX architecture.

Understanding of CI/CD pipelines, configuration as code - Terraform Security Awareness: Solid understanding of SAML 2.0, OIDC, SSO, and identity management concepts RISE: Understanding of the RISE with SAP operating model and SAP Cloud ALM.

Soft Skills & Behaviours Visionary yet pragmatic: Balances long-term architecture ambition with short-term delivery reality (strategic vs. tactical). Strong conviction with open mind: Defends architectural principles but listens to field constraints.

Excellent communicator: Explains complex architecture concepts to business stakeholders, product teams, and technical audiences alike. Collaborative authority: Influences without commanding; earns trust through expertise. Works with security, operations, and enterprise architecture - not in place of them.

Systems thinking: Sees the whole SAP landscape as interconnected and integrated within a global, heterogeneous enterprise landscape. Never forgets the Enterprise Architecture guiding principles. Intellectual curiosity: Continuously tracks SAP innovation and industry best practices.

s.h: ## WHAT YOU'LL LOVE ABOUT WORKING HERE ##

s.t:
Eraneos ist eine internationale Beratungsgruppe für Strategie, Transformation und Technologie, die Unternehmen dabei unterstützt, in einer dynamischen digitalen Welt erfolgreich zu sein.

Mit erstklassigen Expertinnen und Experten aus Business und Technologie befähigen wir unsere Kunden, neue Massstäbe für nachhaltige Transformationen zu setzen - von der Strategie bis zur Umsetzung.

Ob bei der Gestaltung zukunftsfähiger Organisationen, der Erschliessung neuer Potenziale durch Daten und KI oder der Absicherung von Unternehmen durch ganzheitliche Cybersicherheit: Wir liefern Resultate pragmatisch und zielgerichtet.

Unser Team von rund 1-200 engagierten Mitarbeitenden ist in Büros in der Schweiz, Deutschland, den Niederlanden, Spanien, Dänemark, Schweden, Österreich, Grossbritannien, Singapur und den USA vertreten und verbindet globale Perspektiven mit starken lokalen Wurzeln.

An den Schweizer Standorten Zürich, Bern und Lausanne arbeiten rund 450 Mitarbeitende.
# **Das ist der Job - Deine Hauptaufgaben** #
* Du entwickelst tragfähige Data- & AI-Lösungsarchitekturen. Gemeinsam mit Fachbereichen, IT und Delivery Lead konkretisierst du Anforderungen und übersetzt sie in umsetzbare Konzepte. Du wägst Standardprodukte, Managed Services und Eigenentwicklungen gegeneinander ab.
* Du gestaltest das Zusammenspiel der gesamten Lösung. Du verbindest Daten, AI-Modelle, Anwendungen, Schnittstellen und Infrastruktur und entwickelst Sicherheits-, Berechtigungs-, Deployment\- und Betriebskonzepte für Cloud-, On-Prem- und hybride Umgebungen.
* Du arbeitest selbst an der technischen Umsetzung. Du überprüfst kritische Annahmen durch technische Spikes und Prototypen, implementierst anspruchsvolle Komponenten und begleitest die Lösung bis zum produktiven Einsatz.
* Du machst AI-Lösungen produktionsreif. Du definierst mit dem Team Anforderungen an Tests, Evaluation, Monitoring und Betrieb und wägst Qualität, Performance, Verfügbarkeit und Gesamtkosten gegeneinander ab.
* Du übernimmst technische Führung. Du setzt Engineering-Standards, führst Code- und Architekturreviews durch und coachst Engineers. Dabei entwickelst du auch den qualitätsgesicherten Einsatz von AI im Software Development Lifecycle weiter.
* Du berätst Kunden und vertrittst technische Entscheidungen. Du moderierst Lösungs- und Architekturworkshops, erklärst Alternativen und deren Konsequenzen und stimmst Architektur, Security und Betrieb mit den zuständigen Fachpersonen ab.
# **Dieser Job ist für dich, wenn** #
* Praktische Erfahrung mit produktiven AI-Lösungen im Enterprise-Umfeld. Du hast Lösungen selbst entworfen und implementiert und kennst Entwicklung, Deployment und Betrieb aus eigener Erfahrung.
* Fundierte Kenntnisse in Agentic AI und modernen AI-Architekturen. Du verstehst Agents, Agent-Teams und deren Orchestrierung, Tool-Calling, strukturierte Ausgaben sowie multimodale Verarbeitung mit Voice und Vision.
* Technische Tiefe in Software und Daten. Du beherrschst Service- und API-Design und verstehst Datenmodelle, Datenflüsse, Fachsystemintegration, asynchrone Verarbeitung und verteilte Systeme.
* Erfahrung mit Cloud, On-Prem, Managed Services, Modellbereitstellung, Netzwerk und Infrastrukturautomatisierung.
* Ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Sicherheit und Produktionsreife. Du berücksichtigst Identitäten, Rollen, Datenzugriffe, Secrets und Auditierbarkeit ebenso wie AI-spezifische Risiken. Tests, CI/CD, Observability, Versionierung und Wiederanlauf gehören für dich zur Lösungsarchitektur.
* Beratungskompetenz und Freude am People Business, sowie sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens C1-Niveau.
# **Als i-Tüpfelchen bringst du mit ** #
* Erfahrung mit anspruchsvollen Betriebsumgebungen: Du hast lokale Modellbereitstellung, GPU-Infrastruktur oder Lösungen mit besonderen Anforderungen an Datenschutz, Verfügbarkeit oder Isolation realisiert.
* Erfahrung mit strukturierter Architekturdokumentation: Du nutzt beispielsweise arc42 und dokumentierst Architekturentscheidungen so, dass Kunden und Umsetzungsteams damit weiterarbeiten können.
* Erfahrung mit AI-gestütztem Engineering: Du hast Coding-Assistenten und Agents über die persönliche Nutzung hinaus in Entwicklungs-, Review- und Testprozesse integriert und deren Qualität abgesichert.
* Erfahrung mit Wiederverwendung und Presales: Du hast Referenzarchitekturen oder gemeinsame Komponenten aufgebaut oder durch technische Beratung und überzeugende Lösungsentwürfe zur Gewinnung neuer Mandate beigetragen.
Auch wenn nicht alle Anforderungen vollständig erfüllt sind, freuen wir uns sehr über eine Bewerbung.
# **Dein nächster Schritt zur erfolgreichen Bewerbung** #
* Hüseyin als deine Ansprechperson freut sich auf deine Direktbewerbung über unsere Webseite (Lebenslauf, Diplome und Arbeitszeugnisse in PDF).
Diversity wird bei uns grossgeschrieben - zeig uns, was dich ausmacht, und schick uns deine Unterlagen noch heute!
*Bewerbungen per E-Mail sowie von Personaldienstleistern werden nicht berücksichtigt und direkt gelöscht.*

Are you a systems architect or senior engineer who has built the digital backbone of a manufacturing or high-tech company, ready to own it end-to-end? At Lightium, we are building next-generation photonic integrated circuits (PICs) based on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), and we are looking for an Enterprise Data & Systems Architect to become the technical backbone of our data platform and enterprise systems.

We seek a hands-on Enterprise Data & Systems Architect to own the technical architecture of our data infrastructure, automation and digital systems. The ownership spans from database architecture and data warehouse to PLM, ERP and MES systems, as well as test automation, serving both R&D and growing production flow.

As part of the Operations team, you will drive the data and systems strategy, own the integration between tools and data infrastructure, keeping the landscape coherent and lean as we scale from pilot to volume production. You will be managing and mentoring a small team of specialists ranging from DevOps to Data Scientists and Automation Engineers.

Enterprise Systems Architecture & Strategy: Own the architecture and roadmap for Lightium’s data platform, enterprise systems, and supporting infrastructure as we scale from pilot to volume.

Ensure that decisions across the data warehouse, PLM, ERP, MES, and HW/SW infrastructure reinforce one another rather than compete, and translate manufacturing and business needs into a coherent, pragmatic systems strategy that ensures data traceability across the company and across multiple locations and departments.

Build and maintain high level dashboards that allows both operations and leadership teams to track KPI. Be responsible for all the cloud computing and cloud storage solutions, including Azure, AWS, Google Computing (GC) to ensure a cost-effective and scalable operations for both simulations, data analysis and data storage.
Data & Analytics Platform: Own the database and data-warehouse architecture and the modeling of test and manufacturing data, scaling it to support higher production volumes. Design, build, and operate the databases, data pipelines, transformation and orchestration, and lakehouse behind it on a modern data stack.

Set the data contracts, naming conventions, and quality standards that keep data trustworthy and traceable as volume grows, and ensure the platform powers reliable analytics, BI, reporting, and internal tools at scale.
Data Security, Governance & Compliance: Own IT and data security and governance across the platform: access control (including external and internal Tier-based access), managing data encryption in transit and at rest, backups and disaster recovery, and clear ownership of who can access what.

Align the systems and data landscape with the relevant standards (ISO 9001 quality management and ISO/IEC 27001 information security) and design the access and data-segregation controls that ensures confidentiality, and support export-control compliance (ITAR, US EAR, and the Swiss Goods Control Act / dual-use regulations) when handling sensitive PIC technical data.
Enterprise Systems & Product Lifecycle: Own Aras Innovator (PLM) and the ERP (Oracle NetSuite) implementation, including ongoing rollout, configuration, and the integration between the two. Drive end-to-end product and document lifecycle traceability, from design through to manufacturing, measurements, reporting and shipment, and keep master data consistent and clean across systems.
MES Selection & Implementation: Scout the market for a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) platform that fits both R&D (with high flexibility) and production (with high scalability), and run the full supplier tender through to vendor selection. Lead the subsequent implementation and integration of the MES with PLM, ERP, and the data platform, so that process steps, run data, and traceability flow end-to-end as production scales.
Test Automation & Tool Integration: Own the automated wafer-scale test software built on OpenTAP, from architecture and build through production rollout. Define and maintain the data-exchange protocols between tools and systems, connecting PLM, ERP, test, MES, and the data warehouse, and partner with process and test engineering to keep automation reliable and scalable as production volume ramps.
Infrastructure, Vendors & Continuous Improvement: Own the reliability, security, and scaling of core infrastructure (Linux servers, virtualization, containerized services, object storage, and backups), from the lakehouse and storage layers to application hosting and manufacturing-adjacent systems, and manage projects, contracts, and SLAs with external IT vendors and managed-service providers.

Document architecture as living references, support the colleagues who use the systems day to day, and continuously improve how data and digital tools serve the company.
Technical Guidance & Mentorship: Act as the technical reference and architect for the wider engineering community, setting the direction, standards, and best practices that automation engineers, data and analytics engineers, DevOps engineers, and interns. Manage and mentor a small team of specialists, and guide them in their day-to-day work, and support the hiring process for these roles as the team grows around the architecture you define.

Educational Background: A degree in computer science, engineering, physics, or a related field, with a strong track record in enterprise or solutions architecture, ideally in a manufacturing or semiconductor environment. You have ideally designed and built enterprise systems architectures from scratch.
Technical Expertise: Hands-on experience with PLM (Aras Innovator or similar) and ERP systems, including their implementation and integration. A track record leading automated/robotic production or testing lines, preferably in a semiconductor industry or similar.

A strong database and data-engineering background (database and data-model design, data pipelines, transformation and orchestration, and data quality), hands-on with modern lakehouse and data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Iceberg, and Trino, and comfortable across both cloud and on-prem infrastructure, including containers, object storage, and lakehouse architectures.

A solid grasp of data security, encryption, backups, and access control. Vendor and contract management experience, including negotiating SLAs with managed-service providers. Familiarity with data-relevant standards (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001) and export-control regimes (ITAR, US EAR, Swiss dual-use / Goods Control Act) is a strong asset.

Proficiency in modern AI solutions.
Mindset: Pragmatic and lean by instinct, happy to architect and to build with your own hands, and to solve problems through smart integration and vendor orchestration rather than headcount. People-leadership experience, with a track record of hiring, managing and mentoring technical staff. A strong communicator, able to translate manufacturing and business needs into technical strategy for executive leadership, and at home in a fast-moving startup.

As an Enterprise Solutions Architect at ClickHouse, you'll own the technical side of the sales cycle for enterprise accounts. You'll engage with data platform engineers, architects, SRE, and the VP who owns the standard — and your job is to design something that satisfies all of them and then prove it at production scale.
Getting an enterprise team there usually means moving them off something else, so most of your work is making that migration credible: the architecture, benchmarks run against their own data, and a plan their engineers believe they can execute.
This is a role for engineers who want the hard version of the problem: real scale, real constraints, and an incumbent to displace. Prior pre-sales experience helps but isn't required — technical depth is non-negotiable.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the technical evaluation for enterprise accounts — from discovery through POC or competitive bake-off, architecture sign-off, security review, and first production workload.
Engage across a wider set of stakeholders than a single team: data platform engineers, architects, SRE, security, and the executive who owns the standard. Design solutions that hold up with all of them in the room.
Design for production scale — sizing, sharding and replication strategy, ingestion topology, tiered storage, cost modeling, and what happens when something fails at 3am.
Win competitive displacements against Elasticsearch, Splunk, Snowflake, BigQuery, Druid, Pinot, and homegrown systems, using benchmarks the customer's own team can reproduce.
Own the migration plan — sequencing, dual-run, validation, and cutover — so the customer's team can see exactly how they get to production.
Clear the security and procurement path: questionnaires, compliance artifacts, network and identity architecture, and BYOC or private deployment requirements.
Partner closely with Enterprise AEs to progress and close opportunities — you own the technical win, they own the commercial close. Build the TCO case against the incumbent/competition together.
Advocate for customer needs internally with Product and Engineering — you're the voice of the technical buyer inside ClickHouse.
Contribute reference architectures, benchmark harnesses, migration guides, and objection handling material that help the team scale what's working.

Deep technical foundation in data infrastructure — built through experience as a data engineer, platform engineer, software engineer, DBA, or solutions architect.
Production experience with analytical databases (ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Druid, Pinot, Vertica) and with operating them, not just querying them.
Distributed systems judgment: partitioning, replication, consistency trade-offs, query execution, and a felt sense for where things break under load.
Fluency across the modern data stack — Kafka and CDC pipelines, orchestration, object storage, BI tools, and at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) at architecture level.
Experience running a technical evaluation against a named competitor and winning it, including designing the migration off the incumbent and the parts of it that are genuinely hard.
Customer-facing experience with real stakes — pre-sales, consulting, technical account management, or a staff-level engineering role that put you in front of customers.
Strong written and verbal communication. You can whiteboard with a staff engineer in the morning and present to a VP of Engineering in the afternoon.
Comfort with longer cycles and more stakeholders. Enterprise evaluations don't close in three weeks, and you know how to keep one moving without letting it stall.
Willingness to say ClickHouse isn't the right tool for a given workload when that's true.

The SaaS and Software Governance team sits within Corporate IT and helps OpenAI scale from startup-speed tooling to mature enterprise architecture. The team owns practical governance for software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, identity, data access, and agent-enabled workflows, with a mandate to improve security, reduce software sprawl, and help business teams move faster through better foundations.

OpenAI is scaling from an emerging, high-velocity startup into a mature enterprise operating model. The IT Software Architect will help shape the software, SaaS, Data integration, and agent-enabled architecture that lets the company move quickly while improving security, compliance, data quality, and customer, partner, and employee experience.
This role is not a traditional ivory-tower architecture function. It is a hands-on governance and enablement role that partners with business teams, IT operations, Security, Procurement, Business Platforms, Applied teams and Data Engineering to guide software decisions, reduce unmanaged sprawl, and build reusable enterprise foundations.
Why This Role Matters
OpenAI’s software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI. The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy.
The person in this role will help turn software governance from an approval checkpoint into an enterprise capability: a system that improves speed, reliability, security, and business outcomes.

Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT. Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software.
Build lightweight governance patterns that guide teams before software and integration decisions become hard to unwind.
Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration.
Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness.
Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions.
Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns.
Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit.
Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration.
Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools.
Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners.
Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model.
Core Architecture Domains
SaaS governance and software catalog maturity
Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries
Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users
Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models.
Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns
Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms.
Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness
Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management

OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology.

You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.
The Operating Systems team is critical in this mission, turning sophisticated hardware and AI capabilities into a reliable, trusted platform. Security is central to that work: we define trust boundaries, integrate hardware-backed protections, isolate sensitive context, and establish the guardrails that let AI applications and agents act safely, privately, and under user control.

We’re looking for a Software Security Architect to define the security architecture for OpenAI’s next-generation operating system. You’ll work alongside hardware security architects and partner with operating system, silicon, firmware, privacy, and product teams to protect users, their devices, and their data.
This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. Your work will shape the platform’s trust model, protect sensitive information, and set the technical foundations for AI that is safe, private, and under user control.

Define the operating system’s security architecture, trust boundaries, privilege model, and protections for sensitive user data.
Partner with hardware security architects to integrate roots of trust, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and processor security capabilities into the operating system.
Design foundational platform defenses, including secure boot, code signing, attestation, secure updates, key protection, and device recovery.
Establish isolation and access controls across the kernel, applications, system services, and AI workloads.
Define guardrails for how AI applications and agents access information, use sensors and tools, retain context, and act on a user’s behalf.
Lead threat modeling and architecture reviews across the platform, translating emerging threats into practical, enforceable requirements.
Prototype solutions, review security-critical systems code, and guide engineering teams through complex technical and product tradeoffs.

Deep experience designing or securing operating systems, kernels, embedded platforms, hypervisors, or other privileged systems software.
Complex understanding of operating system internals, including memory protection, process isolation, executable loading, device drivers, and privilege boundaries.
Experience building security architectures that span hardware, firmware, operating systems, applications, and cloud services.

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is building and productizing infrastructure capabilities that help organizations deploy and operate advanced AI systems at scale. The team works across AI hardware, systems engineering, physical infrastructure, and customer delivery to turn emerging technologies into reliable, repeatable infrastructure solutions.
Our work sits at the intersection of technical strategy, product development, engineering, and deployment. We partner closely with customers and internal engineering teams to solve complex infrastructure challenges spanning compute, power, cooling, controls, and facility efficiency.

We are seeking a senior, hands-on Data Center Infrastructure Architect to develop and optimize the physical infrastructure required for large-scale AI deployments.
This is a broad technical role spanning data center architecture, electrical and mechanical systems, high-density compute, controls, telemetry, and digital modeling. You will use simulation, operational data, and digital-twin approaches to evaluate infrastructure designs, identify system-level constraints, and improve efficiency, reliability, cost, and speed of deployment.
The ideal candidate can move fluidly between first-principles analysis, facility and equipment design, computational modeling, engineering review, and real-world implementation. You should be comfortable working across disciplines rather than operating solely within electrical, mechanical, or software boundaries.

Define system-level architectures for high-density AI data centers across power, cooling, IT equipment, controls, and facility infrastructure.
Develop digital twins and other computational models that represent the behavior of data center systems under changing workloads, environmental conditions, equipment configurations, and failure scenarios.
Use design and operational data to identify constraints, improve PUE and related efficiency metrics, and optimize capacity, reliability, water consumption, cost, and deployment schedules.
Evaluate tradeoffs across electrical topology, cooling architecture, rack density, redundancy, controls, maintainability, constructability, and operational complexity.
Translate evolving AI hardware requirements into practical facility, rack, power, and thermal architectures.
Establish reference architectures, modeling standards, design assumptions, performance requirements, and validation methodologies that can be reused across customer deployments.
Partner with software, data, controls, hardware, mechanical, electrical, construction, commissioning, and operations teams to connect digital models with real infrastructure behavior.
Integrate telemetry from systems such as BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, equipment controllers, and IT hardware into modeling and optimization workflows.
Lead technical reviews of customer and partner designs, identify material risks, and recommend changes grounded in quantitative analysis.
Work with customers and delivery teams to adapt reference solutions to site-specific constraints while preserving performance, reliability, and efficiency objectives.
Support pilots, commissioning, performance testing, and post-deployment analysis to validate models and continuously improve infrastructure designs.
Help shape the technical roadmap for Industrial Compute’s physical-infrastructure products and engineering services.

Significant experience designing or optimizing hyperscale data centers, large mission-critical facilities, or comparable infrastructure systems.

Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

We are looking for an AI Agent Security Architect to function as the primary technical authority for Replit’s autonomous and AI agent security blueprint.

In this critical role, you will design, implement, and maintain the runtime defense systems, guardrail frameworks, and sandboxing architectures that govern AI agents executing code, invoking tools, and reasoning across our platform.

You will be a key technical contributor—leading high-impact AI security initiatives and bridging the gap between non-deterministic AI behavior and rigorous cybersecurity controls for both engineering and executive leadership.

AI Agent Security Strategy & Technical Execution
AI Agent Security Blueprint: Define the long-term vision and architectural patterns for securing autonomous agent workflows, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, multi-turn reasoning loops, and multi-agent coordination.
Runtime Guardrails & Policy Enforcement: Architect and deploy dynamic input/output guardrail systems, semantic firewalls, and real-time intent verification filters to prevent goal hijacking, system prompt leaks, and indirect prompt injections.
Agent Execution & Tool Sandboxing: Partner with Infrastructure and AppSec teams to design secure, short-lived, micro-isolated environments (e.g., microVMs, WebAssembly, container sandboxes) where agents can dynamically execute code, run shell commands, and interact with host operating systems safely.
Agentic Threat Modeling & Red Teaming: Conduct specialized threat modeling against non-deterministic systems. Lead automated and manual AI red-teaming initiatives to uncover vulnerabilities in RAG context pipelines, vector stores, and tool-calling interfaces.
Identity, Delegation & Least Privilege: Architect fine-grained permission models and step-up Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) authorization patterns for agents acting on behalf of users—ensuring agents never exceed the delegated privileges of the end user or misuse API keys.
Context & Memory Boundary Security: Design strict data isolation and poisoning prevention controls for vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and long-term conversation memories across multi-tenant workloads.
Risk Management & Cross-Functional Enablement
Maintain the AI Security Source of Truth: Define, document, and maintain authoritative secure design patterns and SDKs for engineering teams building internal or customer-facing AI agent capabilities.
Contribution to Risk Register: Identify, quantify, and document non-deterministic and agentic security risks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs & AI Agents, MITRE ATLAS), ensuring they are accurately represented in the Cybersecurity Risk Register.
Auditability & Observability: Design tamper-evident logging and telemetry standards for agent reasoning chains, tool execution history, and context assembly to support incident response, forensics, and GRC requirements.
Compliance & Sales Enablement: Partner with GRC to translate complex AI security controls into enterprise-ready audit documentation (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act readiness) and support Sales on complex enterprise security inquiries regarding AI safety.

6+ years of experience in security engineering or security architecture, with at least 2+ years dedicated specifically to AI/ML security, LLM application security, or securing agentic frameworks.
Deep understanding of agentic architectures and protocols (e.g., Model Context. Protocol (MCP), LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, ReAct frameworks, and vector database technologies).
Hands-on expertise with threat vectors unique to agentic AI: Indirect Prompt
Injection, Goal Hijacking, Tool Parameter Tampering, Data Poisoning, and Context Contamination.
Strong background in applying safety standards and risk frameworks such as OWASP Top 10 for LLMs & AI Agents, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS.
Proficiency in Python, Go, or TypeScript/JavaScript with a proven track record of reviewing code and building functional security tooling or guardrails.

Exceptional ability to communicate complex non-deterministic AI risks to both deep technical engineers and executive stakeholders.
Proven track record of contributing to an enterprise Cybersecurity Risk Register.
Experience designing runtime sandboxing and isolation technologies (e.g., Firecracker, gVisor, Docker, WebAssembly) for dynamic code execution environments.

The Pre-Sales Solutions Architect (SA) Leader owns the health, direction, and performance of the Solutions Architecture function. Where an individual SA is the technical owner within the sales cycle for their assigned opportunities, the SA Leader is accountable for technical win rate and deal velocity across the entire pre-sales motion — every channel the team supports, and the people who deliver against it.
The SA Leader is a player-coach: they carry direct accountability for channel coverage, the most strategic or highest-stakes evaluations, and cross-functional GTM alignment, while spending the majority of their time developing individual SAs so the team's proactive, commercially-sharp approach scales without becoming order-taking.
Compensation Note: SA Leader compensation is tied to team-wide ARR bookings — new logo, expansion, and multi-year commitments across every SA's pipeline, not just deals the Leader personally works. The Leader is expected to operate with the same commercial mindset as the team, at portfolio scale.

People Leadership & Team Development
The SA Leader hires, coaches, and grows the SA team so each member operates as a credible, commercially sharp technical partner in the sales cycle. This includes:
Hiring and onboarding new SAs, including calibrating them against the channel-specific technical evaluation prompts
Running regular 1:1s, reviewing deal strategy, PoC scoping, and objection handling, and giving direct feedback
Building and maintaining repeatable playbooks (discovery frameworks, PoC templates, objection/RFP responses, competitive positioning) so quality doesn't depend on tenure
Setting and holding the team to a consistent bar for technical depth, commercial instinct, and quota attainment
Channel & Coverage Ownership
The SA Leader owns the coverage model for the entire function — deciding, tracking, and rebalancing which SAs support which channels, and closing gaps as pipeline shifts. This includes accountability across all five channels in the SA Channel Mapping :
Direct Sales (AMER, EMEA, APJ)
Hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI)
Accelerators, Incubators, VCs (YCombinator, TechStars, 500 Startups)
SfP + OAuth Partners (Lovable, Bolt, Anthropic)
Solution Providers ( Postgres.ai , Stormatics)
Rebalancing SA assignment across channels as pipeline volume, deal complexity, or new partner motions shift
Resolving coverage gaps (a channel with no dedicated SA depth, or a region outgrowing its current allocation) and deciding when a hire, a cross-channel reassignment, or a controlled exception is the right fix
Approving which opportunities warrant Leader-level involvement directly, versus staying with the assigned SA
Technical Sales Ownership (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures every significant opportunity has a clear, accountable technical owner across architecture fit, use cases, evaluation criteria, and competitive positioning — spot-checking deal documentation and risk tracking across the pipeline, and stepping in directly on the largest or most strategic evaluations.

The SA Leader ensures the team consistently qualifies opportunities as technically winnable early, coaching SAs on discovery quality and holding the team accountable for surfacing deal-level risk to AEs and sales leadership before it costs a deal.
Proof of Concept and Evaluation Support (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures PoCs across the team are scoped to demonstrate differentiated value, not just technical box-checking — auditing success criteria, evaluation structure, and win-rate patterns across the whole book of active evaluations.
Technical Objection Handling (oversight)
The SA Leader is the escalation layer above the individual SA for the hardest architecture, security, or compliance objections — brought in on RFPs, security questionnaires, and competitive deals that could stall without senior technical input, without replacing the SA as the deal's primary technical contact.
Commercial Technical Alignment (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures the team consistently connects technical requirements to commercial outcomes across the pipeline, and personally engages on pricing/packaging justification and expansion-signal strategy for the largest deals.
Internal Collaboration
Sales (Account Executives)
The SA Leader partners with Sales leadership to make sure SA/AE pairing is working at the portfolio level — owning the technical narrative in aggregate while sales leadership owns the commercial motion — and personally steps in when a specific SA/AE partnership needs adjudicating.
Partnerships
The SA Leader works with Partner Leads across every channel (Hyperscalers, Accelerators, SfP+OAuth, Solution Providers) to make sure SA support scales with each channel's motion, while commercial terms and channel strategy stay owned by the Partner Lead.
Engineering and Product
The SA Leader represents the aggregated market signal — patterns across deals, not just one opportunity — to engineering and product, and prioritizes which recurring technical blockers or roadmap gaps are costing the team deals versus which are one-offs.
Technical Account Management (TAM) and Customer Engineering
The SA Leader ensures handoff quality from pre-sale to post-sale is consistent across the team — auditing that architecture decisions, commitments, and open items are documented well enough that TAMs and CEs can drive early adoption without re-discovering the deal.
Success Metrics
SA Leader effectiveness is measured by commercial and technical outcomes across the whole team, not just their own deals:
Team ARR Bookings — new logo and expansion ARR across every SA's pipeline, relative to team quota
Deal Velocity — time from technical qualification to technical win, tracked across channels
PoC Win Rate — percentage of structured evaluations that convert to closed-won, team-wide
Pipeline Coverage — volume and quality of SA-engaged opportunities relative to quota, per channel
Handoff Quality — post-sale team satisfaction with documentation and deal context, across the team
Team health — ramp time to productivity for new SAs, retention of the SA team itself

Anthropic trains and serves frontier AI models on some of the largest and most diverse accelerator fleets in the world, and the hardware those models run on is one of the most direct levers we have on capability, cost, and reliability. Our Hardware Systems team owns the system-level architecture of that compute — from the package boundary out through boards, racks, interconnect, power, cooling, and the datacenter interface.
We're hiring senior hardware systems architects and technical leads who can work broadly across the hardware stack and go deep where it's needed, and who have the judgment to make and own directional calls — what to build, what to buy, what to co-design with a partner. You'll set architecture, write the specs that partners and internal teams build against, and own the validation and qualification strategy that proves the result.
The skillsets we need span power, cooling, mechanical, interconnect, signal integrity, data and control plane, system management, reliability and serviceability — applied across networking, compute, storage, and accelerator systems.
You'll work closely with our ML performance, infrastructure software, supply chain, and datacenter teams, and directly with hardware vendors and partners across the stack. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a genuine collaborator — we expect this team to push on what AI-assisted hardware design and review can look like.

Own system path-finding and architecture for your domain across the breadth of compute Anthropic deploys — from concept and requirements through spec, design review, and deployment — and act as a reviewer and thought partner across the others.
Write and own high-level requirements and specifications — system, board, interface, rack — that partners and internal teams build against.
Review partner and vendor designs against our requirements, make the build / buy / co-design calls with supply chain and partnership teams, and surface misalignment or schedule risk early enough to act on it.
Drive the interconnect and networking architecture that ties our systems together — scale-up and scale-out fabrics, NICs and switches, optics, and topology.
Drive board-, chassis-, and system-level architecture with our partners — major component placement, PCB architecture, connector and cable design, and power and thermal budgeting — at the chassis, rack, and data-hall level.
Develop performance simulations, hardware models, and "what-if" scenarios to evaluate and choose between candidate hardware architectures.
Define validation, bring-up, and qualification strategy for new platforms — including the telemetry and reliability targets they need to hit in the fleet — and track the technology roadmaps and vendor landscape that shape what we deploy in the short and long term.
Partner with ML performance and infrastructure software teams so hardware decisions land well for the workloads that actually run on them.
Help shape how hardware engineering operates at Anthropic — develop and apply AI-assisted approaches to design, spec review, and validation; establish review forums, spec standards, and partner engagement.

Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one core hardware-systems domain (e.g., interconnect, power, thermal) for large-scale compute or networking systems.
Experience owning hardware system architecture at scale — machine, rack, row, and cluster — and authoring specifications and requirements.
Experience taking hardware from architecture through bring-up and high-volume production deployment.
Experience working with external hardware vendors and partners — reviewing their designs and holding them to a specification.
Ability to reason about trade-offs across adjacent hardware domains (e.g., interconnect ↔ power ↔ thermal ↔ mechanical) rather than within a single one.
Track record of technical leadership — owning directional decisions and their consequences, and driving alignment across teams and partners.
Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
Strong written communication — you'll write specs and reviews that many teams depend on.

8+ years in hardware systems architecture or engineering for hyperscale, HPC, AI/ML, or high-end networking platforms.
Experience with AI accelerator systems (GPU, TPU, or other custom ASIC platforms) and their scale-up / scale-out fabrics.
Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and co-design.
Experience establishing a new function, program, or engineering practice.
Comfort working with — and curiosity about pushing — AI tools as part of an engineering workflow.
Degree in EE, CE, ME, CS, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

s.h: Depth in one or more of
s.t:
High-speed SerDes, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet/InfiniBand, and optical interconnect.
BMC and platform firmware, hardware root of trust, and secure boot.
48V/HVDC power delivery and direct liquid cooling.
Fleet-scale reliability engineering and RAS architecture.
Signal and power integrity.
Representative projects
Define the scale-up and scale-out interconnect architecture for a next-generation training platform, from link budget and topology through switch / NIC / optics selection and the bring-up and validation plan.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. As the Manager of Commercial Applied AI Architects at Anthropic, you will drive adoption of frontier AI across our mid-market and SMB customers by leading a team of technical architects who help companies build and deploy with the Claude API, Claude Code, the Agent SDK, and Claude for Enterprise.

Commercial is one of Anthropic's largest and fastest-moving books of business: thousands of companies, a rapidly growing sales team, and a small group of architects whose job is to change deal outcomes where technical depth matters most. Your team's leverage does not come from being everywhere.

It comes from choosing the right accounts to go deep on, then turning what they learn there into blueprints, demos, tooling, and enablement that reach the rest of the book.
You will bring your own builder credibility and technical judgment to the role. Our architects ship working code: prototypes, eval frameworks, near-production examples that customers extend, and internal tooling that scales the team itself.

You do not need to be the strongest engineer in the room, but you should expect to be in the work with your team, not just reviewing it from above. When an architect is deep in a hard engagement, you will often be right there alongside them, unblocking, pairing, and pressure-testing, while the account itself stays theirs.
This is a first-line leadership role reporting to the Head of Applied AI, Commercial. You will start by managing a team of architects and are expected to help grow it well beyond its current size, partnering with Commercial sales leadership on coverage, qualification, and where technical investment pays off. You will co-own the strategy for how Applied AI shows up in the Commercial segment, and you will be judged on your team's outcomes and growth, not your own.

Claude Code is changing how engineering organizations build software, and most of them need someone to show them how. That's you.
Technical Architects help customers get real work done with Claude Code, Claude Tag (Claude Code as an agent in Slack), and the enterprise admin controls that decide whether a rollout succeeds. You'll teach customers, partners and Anthropic's own field teams. Just as important, you'll train the trainers who carry that knowledge to everyone else.
We're hands-on AI engineers who would rather teach than sell. You'll work alongside customer engineering organizations, teaching them about Claude Code and shepherding rollouts with advanced admin knowledge. Most weeks you're in front of an audience with Claude Desktop or a terminal open: thousands of engineers on a public webinar one day, a customer's platform team in their own conference room the next week, office hours in between. The prep material often reaches you the day before.
The team is growing quickly this year, scope will grow as new products ship, and the people who join now will shape how it works.

Teach in every format. Take a standing rotation on Anthropic's public webinars in front of thousands of engineers at a time. Lead workshops and multi-day onsites, in person and virtual, built around a customer's own codebase and questions. Host office hours and multi-week cohorts where engineers, partners, and account teams bring live problems.
Teach the teachers. Run train-the-trainer programs for customer technologists and champions, and certify them to deliver Anthropic's material.
Empower admins. Educate enterprise admins on the technical requirements for a strong rollout by guiding them through single sign-on, permissions, connectors, spend controls, data-handling policy, and other advanced topics.
Build fast with Claude. Turn a request into a polished deck, demo repository or plugin within a day, using the tools you teach. Explore new features the day they ship. Pick up a teammate's material and deliver it as if you wrote it.
Bring field signal back to product. Tell the Claude Code, Claude Tag and Cowork teams what customers run into, specifically enough that they can fix it.
Be the technical voice in the room. Partner with account executives, customer success managers, Applied AI Architects, support engineers and partner leads.
Travel. Expect 30 to 50%, in bursts around onsites, workshops and events.

Range in one conversation. You can go from banter to a rigorous design discussion, and both feel natural.

Initiative. You build things without waiting for permission, and you say when an idea is half-formed, including your manager's.
Steadiness when priorities shift, timelines are short and colleagues are under pressure.
Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving industry and product suite.
